title: Integrate AMD Fidelity FX SDK & FSR integration refactor
body:
This PR is a refactor of the current FSR integration in Godot. Currently, Godot integrates FSR 1 and 2 separately. 
As an alternative, this PR integrates AMD Fidelity FX SDK (abbr. FFX SDK), which provides a common interface for all FFX effects (including FSR 1/2/3 and more). With the use of FFX SDK we could share a common codebase across the integration of all FFX effects.  

## Contents
In particular this PR removes the separately-included FSR 1/2 repositories in `thirdparty` and adds `amd-ffx`, which is based on AMD Fidelity FX SDK 1.1.4 (newer versions no longer provide GLSL sources). This would bring: 
 - FSR 1.0 updated to FSR 1.2.0
 - FSR 2.2.1 (Updated May 2023) updated to FSR 2.3.3 (Updated May 2025)
 - FSR 3.1.4 (both upscaler and frame interpolation) all required sources included, though not integrated with Godot yet, but this provides a good basis for adding FSR 3 integration. 

On the Godot side, the following refactors are done: 
 - Remove `amd-fsr` and `amd-fsr2` third party repositories in favor of the unified `amd-ffx` repo
 - Extract all common interop code with FFX (mainly graphics device interfaces and abstractions) from FSR2 into `FFXCommonContext` so that they could be shared between FSR 1, 2 and 3 (in the future). This reduces FSR integration code almost by half. 
 - Expose a common Godot-FidelityFX interop interface so that integrating Fidelity FX effects (such as the FSR series) become a lot easier and require far less adapting code. 
 - Based on the common interface, refactor the current FSR1 integration to let it leverage the new unified interface, so now it shares a common basis as the FSR2 (and upcoming FSR3) integration. 

## Significance
This PR provide updates for existing FSR versions and provides a good basis for implementing an integration to any new FFX effects. With the common FFX interop code extracted, we can now integrate a new FFX effect with no more than 300~400 LoC. 

## Test
Tested on Windows. Build and run are both OK. The refactors doesn't break the visual effects of FSR 1 and 2.  
If it's convenient, I would like to invite the original author of FSR2 integration (@DarioSamo ) to have a review :)

## Tasks
 - [X] Add Fidelity FX to thirdparty packages and remove `amd-fsr` & `amd-fsr2`
 - [X] Create common Godot-FidelityFX interop interface
 - [X] Refactor FSR1 and FSR2 to let it use the new interface introduced above
 - [X] Integrate FSR3 Upscaler based on this new interface, through #111631 . 

## Future
In a future, I would also consider integrating FSR 3 Frame interpolation (<https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/8768>), which could also benefit from this refactor, but that needs hacking into the swapchain so it may be a bit more complicated than the Upscaler part.  
Since implementing FSR3 Frame gen would require modifying the Godot renderer infrastructure, which will be too complicated for this PR. And that FSR3 Upscaler and FSR frame gen is actually fully decoupled, Upscaler have no dependencies on Frame gen, so this PR would only implement Upscaler. Frame gen would deserve a separate PR.
